title: Judge Conflicting Sources
scenario: It is 6:05 AM. The overnight source is not one note this morning - it is two, and they disagree. Before intake touches anything, make the judgment calls a source conflict demands: who wins, what happens to the loser, and what to do about the fact neither note mentions.
input:
[5:40 AM] Overnight Desk Analyst:
ERCOT spiked overnight. Peak around $204/MWh, settled near $155. Trader flagged the spike for review.

[6:05 AM] Overnight Desk Analyst:
Correction after final settlement: ERCOT peak confirmed at $204/MWh, settled at $151/MWh. No word yet on generation performance.

Desk rule on file: when notes conflict, the later note is authoritative. Every note is captured with its timestamp.
instructions: Read both notes and the desk rule.
Validate to record the conflict profile.

questions.prompt: The notes disagree on the settled price (155 vs 151). What decides which value wins?

options.text: The governed desk rule: the later note is authoritative
The higher price, to be safe
Whichever value the reader finds more plausible

questions.explain: The input states the rule on file. Conflicts are resolved by governance decided in advance - not by caution or plausibility in the moment.

questions.prompt: What makes the later-wins rule safe to AUTOMATE?

options.text: Every note is captured with a timestamp, so later is machine-decidable
The rule only runs when a human is watching

questions.explain: Re-read the last line of the input: a rule is only automatable when the fact it depends on (arrival order) is captured as data.

questions.prompt: Neither note reports generation performance. What should intake record?

options.text: Yesterday's generation status, as the best available guess
Nothing - omit the field entirely and hope nobody notices
An explicit null: checked, and unknown

questions.explain: A guess is an undetectable lie and a silently omitted field is ambiguous. An explicit null tells downstream steps the fact was checked and is genuinely unknown.

questions.prompt: After the correction, what happens to the 5:40 note?

options.text: Delete it so nobody uses the wrong number
Retain it unchanged - superseded sources are audit evidence
Edit it in place so both notes agree

questions.explain: Provenance means keeping what actually happened. Deleting or editing history makes the correction itself unexplainable later.

artifactOnPass.authorityRule: later note wins (governed desk rule, timestamp-decidable)
artifactOnPass.missingFact: generation performance -> recorded as explicit null

copilotPrompt: Judge this source conflict: which note wins and under what rule, what makes the rule automatable, what to record when a fact is stated nowhere, and what happens to the superseded note.
successMessage: Conflict judged. Intake can now build the record knowing which source wins and why.

intro.heading: Before you judge: conflict is the normal case

sections.title: Sources disagree constantly
sections.body: Corrections, retractions, and follow-ups are how human sources actually behave. A workflow that assumes one clean note per morning breaks the first time reality arrives twice.

sections.title: Authority is decided before the conflict
sections.body: Later-wins is not obvious - a desk could reasonably rule that only a NAMED correction supersedes. What matters is that the rule was agreed in advance and depends on captured data (timestamps), so a machine can apply it.

sections.title: Three fates for information
sections.body: This morning produces all three: a value that wins (151), a value that is superseded but retained (155), and a fact that is absent and recorded as null. Knowing which is which IS the inspection skill at this tier.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: By hand you'd copy the analyst's email or chat note and hand-key the ticker, direction, and rationale into named columns so later steps read fields, not prose.

bestFit.how: 'When a new email arrives (V3)' on the desk mailbox, filtered to the overnight sender
a Watch Emails module polling the shared mailbox on a schedule
the graph entry node, with the note text as the first state value to be parsed

takeaway.heading: Conflict profile recorded
points: You resolved a source conflict with a governed, timestamp-decidable rule instead of judgment in the moment.
You assigned the three fates correctly: winning value, retained superseded value, explicit null.
You kept the superseded note as audit evidence - history stays intact even when it is wrong.
The intake build on this tier applies exactly these judgments to produce the record.
The workflow can now decide which source to trust before any extraction happens.
